biography.title: His Life Story
biography.subtitle: The Life of Kanagala Balarama Krishna

01.title: His Early Life
01.content: Kanagala Balarama Krishna was born on 24 December 1965 in Bhattiprolu, Guntur District, into a middle-class family. He was the youngest child of Late Sri Kanagala Venkata Subba Rao and Late Smt. Kanagala Vijaya Mahalaxmi. He spent his childhood in Bhattiprolu and completed his primary and secondary education at Tamanna Mallikarjuna Rao High School, Bhattiprolu, up to the 10th class. Alongside his academics, he was also an NCC cadet, an experience that introduced him to discipline, responsibility and a sense of service from an early age. He completed his matriculation around 1980.

images.caption: His beloved parents - Late Sri Kanagala Venkata Subba Rao and Late Smt. Kanagala Vijaya Mahalaxmi. Balarama Krishna was their youngest son.
After completing his matriculation (10th class) around 1980.

02.title: A Dream of Serving the Nation
02.content: Like many young men of his generation, Balarama Krishna carried a dream of serving the country by joining the Indian Army. He made an attempt to pursue that dream, but fate had other plans. A small fracture prevented him from fulfilling the physical requirements and brought an unexpected end to his aspirations of joining the Army. Although that particular dream could not become a reality, the qualities behind it—his discipline, determination and willingness to serve—remained a part of the person he became. He then turned his attention toward learning a practical skill that would shape the rest of his working life.

03.title: Finding His Path
03.content: After completing his schooling, Balarama Krishna began learning electrical work under the guidance of his elder brother. What began as learning a trade gradually became his profession and his means of supporting his family. He went on to work as a private electrician, dedicating decades of his life to his profession. Through his skill, reliability and hard work, he became familiar to many families in and around Bhattiprolu. His profession connected him with people from different walks of life and became one of the ways through which he built lasting relationships within the community.
03.caption: Beginning his journey as an electrician.

04.title: Family
04.content: On 7 February 1999, Balarama Krishna married Smt. Kanagala Krishna Durga Suneetha. Together, they built their family and were blessed with two sons. As a husband and father, he carried the responsibilities of his family with dedication. He was the family's primary breadwinner and worked consistently to provide for and support those he loved. His work was not simply a profession—it was one of the ways through which he expressed his responsibility toward his family

images.caption: The sacred vratam ceremony after marriage.
With his beloved wife Smt. Kanagala Krishna Durga Suneetha.
Blessed with two sons - a complete family.

05.title: A Man Known Through Relationships
05.content: Beyond his profession and responsibilities as a family man, Balarama Krishna was known for something even more meaningful—the relationships he built with people. He was known as a truthful and straightforward person, and the people of his village developed a deep affection and respect for him. Interestingly, many people in the village did not address him by his name at all. Depending on their relationship with him, they would affectionately call him Babai, Mamayya, Bava, or other familial names. These names reflected something deeper than familiarity. They reflected the place he held in people's lives. To many villagers, he was not simply an electrician or someone they happened to know. He was one of their own—someone they could approach, speak to freely and trust. A large part of the village knew him, and he maintained genuine relationships with people across different generations.

06.title: The Simple Things He Loved
06.content: For all the responsibilities he carried, Balarama Krishna also had his own simple routines and joys. One of the things he loved most was tea. Tea was not simply an occasional drink for him. He had a habit of enjoying it several times throughout the day, and tea shops became familiar places in his everyday routine. He would often sit at a tea shop with a cup of tea and read the daily newspaper, keeping up with the news and happenings around him. These small routines were part of who he was—the ordinary moments that, together, made up the rhythm of his everyday life.

07.title: A Life of Hard Work
07.content: For his family, Balarama Krishna was the person who stood at the forefront of their everyday life—the one who worked hard to bring home their livelihood and ensure that his family was cared for. His profession as a private electrician became a defining part of his life. Through years of dedicated work, he earned the trust of the people who depended on his skills. In 2020, his family moved from Bhattiprolu to Guntur in search of better living conditions and opportunities. Even after moving to Guntur, he continued his work as a private electrician. In a new city, he gradually built another circle of relationships and became known to people there as well. The same qualities that had earned him the affection and trust of people in Bhattiprolu—his honesty, hard work and approachable nature—helped him establish meaningful relationships in Guntur.

08.title: The Life He Built
08.content: From a middle-class childhood in Bhattiprolu to becoming an NCC cadet, a young man who once dreamed of joining the Indian Army, a skilled electrician, a husband, a father, and a person deeply connected to the people around him, Balarama Krishna lived a life shaped by hard work, responsibility, honesty and human relationships. His life was not defined by grand titles or extraordinary possessions. It was defined by the everyday things that matter most—a family he cared for, work he took pride in, responsibilities he carried, people who trusted him, and relationships that extended far beyond his immediate family. For some, he was Babai. For others, Mamayya or Bava. And to his family, he was the person who stood at the heart of their lives. This was the life of Kanagala Balarama Krishna.

finalJourney.title: His Final Chapter
finalJourney.summary: The story of the day he left home, the accident, the hospital, the devastating news, and the final act that followed.

headings.moveLeft: He decided to move towards the left.

day1.title: 3 August 2025 — A Day That Began Like Any Other
day1.content: On 3 August 2025, an ordinary day began in our family. That morning, Mr. Balarama Krishna woke up early. At around 6:00 AM, he completed his morning routine, attended to his personal needs, took his bath, performed his pooja, and then left for work. He left home without having breakfast. He told his wife to prepare breakfast and said that he would return, have it, and then continue with his day. One of the places where he most frequently worked was Stambalagaruvu, Guntur. It was an area where our family had initially settled after moving to Guntur in 2020. By this time, however, we were staying in Krishna Nagar, Guntur. That morning, he went to Stambalagaruvu for work. He had no idea that this ordinary morning would become the final journey of his life.

accident.title: The Accident
accident.content: After completing his work, Balarama Krishna began his journey back home on his bicycle. He was travelling along the third lane of a six-lane, two-way road. While riding on one side of the road, he decided to shift toward the left and move into the adjacent lane. At that exact moment, everything changed. All of a sudden, a car struck the rear tyre of his bicycle. The impact was so strong that he was thrown into the air. He landed on the bonnet of the car, and his head struck the windshield with tremendous force. The impact was severe enough to create a large hole in the windshield of the car. Immediately after the collision, the car driver applied the brakes suddenly. Due to the force generated by the sudden braking, Balarama Krishna was thrown from the bonnet and fell back onto the road. The back of his head struck the road with considerable force. There was not much external bleeding. The car driver and another person immediately got out of the vehicle and tried to help him. At that moment, he was still conscious. When they asked him his name, he was able to respond. They initially tried to call an ambulance. However, they were told that it would take some time to arrive. So they decided to take him to GGH, Guntur, in the same car. During the journey to the hospital, he gradually became drowsy. He slowly began to fall asleep and was snoring. The people accompanying him tried repeatedly to wake him and speak with him so that he would remain conscious until they reached the hospital. When they arrived at GGH, he was moved from the car onto a stretcher and taken into the emergency ward.

news.title: The News Reached Us
news.content: At that time, we knew nothing about what had happened. We were still at home. My mother, unaware of the seriousness of the situation, was actually scolding us, saying something like: 'Even at this age, your father doesn't want to stay at home. He keeps going outside and doing something.' While this conversation was taking place, a stranger came to our home. He told us: 'Babu, your father met with an accident. Don't panic. He has been shifted to the hospital. Go and meet him.' We did not have even a moment to think. Without imagining that anything major had happened, we immediately left for the hospital. At that time, we were thinking that it might be just a small accident—perhaps nothing serious, maybe not even a fracture. We had no idea what awaited us.

ggh.title: At GGH
ggh.content: When we reached the hospital and saw the situation, we were completely shocked. We had no words. We called out: 'Nanna...' He had always responded when we called him—even with a single call. But this time, there was no response. His pulse appeared to be normal. Everything seemed normal from the outside, yet he was not responding to us. The doctors asked us to sign a consent form for high-risk treatment. Our hands were trembling. We were struggling to speak. After he was placed on ventilatory support, he was taken for an MRI scan. After examining him, the doctors told us that his condition was critical. There were no tears at that moment. We were simply holding on to the hope that nothing would happen to him—that somehow he would recover and come back to us normally. After spending several hours at GGH, we decided to move him to a private hospital in the hope of obtaining further specialized treatment.

privateHospital.title: The Private Hospital
privateHospital.content: We took him to a Lalitha super-speciality hospital, where he was admitted to the emergency ward. The necessary tests were performed. By evening, the neurosurgeon and neurologist examined him and reviewed all of his reports. We were still in shock. We were desperately hoping to hear something reassuring from the doctors. Then the doctor came and spoke with us. The words we heard were deeply frightening. The doctor explained that his head had been struck with tremendous force and that there was internal bleeding inside the brain. His condition was extremely serious. The doctor told us that there was approximately a 95% chance that he would not survive. Our hearts broke at those words. It felt as though everything had collapsed in an instant. The doctor told us that they would continue to monitor him until the following morning, holding on to that remaining 5% chance. We prayed for him. We continued to believe that he would come back to us. We held on to hope.

day2.title: 4 August 2025 — The Morning We Never Wanted
day2.content: We did not sleep that night. We waited. We prayed. We kept hoping. Then morning came. It was 4 August 2025. Time continued to pass. Eventually, we were called to speak with the doctors. Our hearts were beating faster and faster. We knew we were about to hear something important, but we were terrified of what those words might be. The Head of the Department of Neurology spoke with us. And then came the words that no family ever wants to hear. She told us: 'We tried in all possible ways, but Mr. Balarama Krishna is not responding. He is brain dead.' With those words, our hearts sank. She explained that a final apnea test would be performed to confirm brain death. After that, we would be allowed to see him. When we entered the ICU and saw him lying there on the ventilator, we broke down completely. We cried like never before. It was impossible to accept what we were seeing.

returnGGH.title: Returning to GGH
returnGGH.content: After that, we spoke with the hospital supervisor. She explained the situation to us and advised us that if we continued to keep him in the private hospital, the hospital expenses would continue to increase, while his organs would gradually deteriorate. She told us that there would be no meaningful benefit in continuing there and asked us to make a decision. With immense pain and sorrow in our hearts, we decided to move him back to the government hospital, GGH, Guntur. We shifted him back to GGH that evening. He was lying on a stretcher with ventilatory support, and we remained beside him with overwhelming grief and pain in our hearts.

night.title: The Night
night.content: At that point, it was difficult to comprehend what was happening. His organs were still functioning. He was physically alive. Yet he was unable to breathe on his own and was not responding to treatment. During the night, his pulse began fluctuating. At times, when the doctors checked with a stethoscope, they could not hear the pulse clearly. Yet when they checked with the ECG, the heartbeat was still being detected. It felt as though he was still fighting to survive. There was no major external wound on his body. There was no significant injury visible anywhere else. The damage was concentrated entirely in his head, with the brain being particularly affected. We kept wishing that somehow this was only a nightmare. We wished that we would wake up and find that none of it had happened. But it wasn't a nightmare. It was real. And this was the final journey of Kanagala Balarama Krishna.

giftOfLife.title: A Selfless Final Act
giftOfLife.summary: The family’s decision, the hope that returned for a moment, and the dignity of a final goodbye that gave others a chance to live.

decision.title: 5 August 2025 — A Decision Born from Love
decision.content: The morning after we had shifted him back to GGH, Guntur, came. It was 5 August 2025. Mr. Balarama Krishna was still on the ventilator. By then, as a family, we were facing a reality that was almost impossible to accept. Although he might no longer be able to live physically with us, we began thinking about something that could give meaning to his life even beyond that moment. We discussed the possibility of donating his organs. Our thought was simple: 'He may not live physically with us, but his organs can continue to function and give a second life to others.' With this thought in our hearts, we decided to donate his organs. We communicated with Jeevandan AP, the organization involved in facilitating organ donation, and expressed our willingness to donate his organs. They obtained the necessary consent from our family for organ donation. Following this, Mr. Balarama Krishna was shifted to Aster Ramesh Super Speciality Hospital for the treatment, monitoring and maintenance of his organs so that they could be donated.

hope.title: A Moment That Gave Us Hope Again
hope.content: At the hospital, the management carefully cleaned and groomed him. When we saw him after he had been cleaned and groomed, something happened inside us. For a moment, we forgot everything that had happened. Seeing him looking clean and cared for once again, we began to hope that perhaps he might still recover and return to us normally. That small moment brought back a hope that we knew was difficult to explain. The hospital management continued to keep him under continuous monitoring and followed the prescribed measures for the maintenance of his organs. He was kept under this monitoring and maintenance for two nights.

finalMorning.title: 7 August 2025 — The Final Morning
finalMorning.content: On 7 August 2025, the operation for organ donation was planned. That morning, we went to the ICU to complete the necessary signatures on the concerned forms. Before leaving, we touched his big toe on his leg once. And then something unexpected happened. His leg moved. He reacted by shaking his leg. For a moment, we were shocked and amazed at the same time. After everything that had happened, seeing even that small movement suddenly made us wonder whether there was still some response from him. We immediately asked the doctors about it. The doctors explained that the movement was a spinal reflex, which can occur even after brain death. We understood what they told us, even though emotionally, that brief movement had affected us deeply.

goodbye.title: The Final Goodbye
goodbye.content: At around 11:00 AM, the doctors began moving him to the operation theatre. Before he was taken inside, our family and all our relatives gave him their final messages and condolences. It was an incredibly painful moment. We watched him being taken away, carrying immense sorrow and pain in our hearts. But alongside that pain was another feeling—immense pride. He was giving others a chance at life. Even though we were losing him, a part of him would continue to live through the lives of others. With that thought, we watched him being taken into the operation theatre.

press.title: A Selfless Act That Reached Beyond Our Family
press.content: The organ donation operation was underway. During this time, the press and media arrived. They spoke with our family and recorded our voice statement about the incident and Mr. Balarama Krishna's selflessness in choosing to donate his organs. What had begun as an unimaginable tragedy for our family had now become a story of generosity and humanity. The decision to donate his organs was not something that erased our pain. But it gave that pain a meaning.

finalMoment.title: 3:33 PM — The Final Moment
finalMoment.content: The operation continued. And at 3:33 PM on 7 August 2025, the doctors officially declared the time of death of Mr. Balarama Krishna. The moment was heartbreaking. Yet, alongside the grief, there was an immense sense of pride in knowing that his selflessness had given others the possibility of a second life.

tribute.title: A Tribute from GGH, Guntur
tribute.content: After his official death was declared, the Superintendent of GGH, Guntur, came to meet our family. In the presence of the press and media channels, the Superintendent felicitated our family and shared his words about the generosity and selflessness of Mr. Balarama Krishna. It was a moment of deep sorrow, but also one of honour. Our family had lost someone irreplaceable. But his final act was one that reached beyond himself. He chose, through his family, to give what could still be given. And in doing so, his life became a gift to others.

felicitation.title: Felicitation & Honouring the Family
felicitation.content: Following the tribute from GGH Guntur, the family was honoured by the Revenue Divisional Officer (RDO) in recognition of their immense and selfless decision to donate Mr. Balarama Krishna's organs. The Revenue Divisional Officer felicitated the family by presenting them with a shawl and a flower bouquet, and expressed heartfelt condolences for the loss of Mr. Balarama Krishna. During the felicitation, the officer shared words of appreciation for Mr. Balarama Krishna's contribution and spoke about the extraordinary decision taken by the family during one of the most difficult moments of their lives. The honour was not merely a formal gesture. It was a recognition of the courage, compassion and selflessness behind the family's decision—a decision that allowed Mr. Balarama Krishna's legacy to continue through the lives he helped save.

organDonation.title: The Lives He Touched
organDonation.intro: Through his generosity and selflessness, Mr. Kanagala Balarama Krishna gave the gift of life to others even after his passing. His donated organs and tissues helped five individuals receive the possibility of a new or restored life.

liver.title: One Liver
liver.description: His liver was donated to give another person an opportunity for a second life.

kidneys.title: Two Kidneys
kidneys.description: Both of his kidneys were donated, giving two individuals the opportunity to receive a second chance at life.

eyes.title: Two Eyes — The Gift of Sight
eyes.description: His two eyes were donated, helping two other individuals receive the gift of vision.

heart.title: His Heart
heart.description: The initial test reports for his heart were positive for donation. However, at the time of the organ-retrieval operation, his heart was found to be not in a condition suitable for donation. Therefore, his heart could not be donated.
heart.lives: Test Positive → Not Suitable at Retrieval

organDonation.summary: In total, through the donation of his liver, two kidneys, and two eyes, Mr. Balarama Krishna helped give five individuals the opportunity for a second life or restored vision. His life came to an end, but his generosity did not. A part of him continues through the lives he helped save.
organDonation.closing: His life ended. His gift of life did not.

jeevandan.title: Acknowledgement of His Selflessness
jeevandan.content: The decision to donate his organs was an act of immense generosity and selflessness by Mr. Kanagala Balarama Krishna and his family. In recognition of this noble act, Jeevandan AP awarded an official Certificate of Appreciation acknowledging his selfless contribution through organ donation. This certificate stands as a formal recognition of an act that transformed a moment of profound loss into an opportunity to give life to others.

jeevandanList.title: Recognized by Jeevandan AP
jeevandanList.content: Jeevandan AP has also recognized Mr. K. Balaramakrishna by including his name and photograph in its official donor list, under its Life Savers — Our Donors section. The official Jeevandan Andhra Pradesh portal maintains a dedicated list recognizing organ donors.
jeevandanList.linkText: View the Jeevandan AP Donors List

lvpei.title: Recognition for His Gift of Sight
lvpei.content: His contribution did not stop with organ donation. His two eyes were also donated, giving two other individuals the opportunity to regain vision. In recognition of this gift of sight, L V Prasad Eye Institute (LVPEI) presented a Certificate of Appreciation acknowledging his eye donation. LVPEI is a comprehensive eye-care institution with an established Eye Banking program and a dedicated eye-donation service.

legacy.title: A Legacy Officially Remembered
legacy.content: These certificates are more than pieces of paper. They are official acknowledgements of a selfless decision—a decision that allowed something meaningful to continue even after his life had ended. His name being remembered among the donors of Jeevandan AP, together with the recognition received for his eye donation, stands as a lasting record of the generosity that defined his final act. His life touched people around him. His final act reached beyond them. And his name now remains recorded among those who gave others the gift of life and sight.

newspaperClippings.title: Newspaper Recognition
newspaperClippings.description: His selfless act of organ donation was recognized by various media outlets, featuring his story in newspapers and news platforms.

legacy.title: His Legacy

values.finalMessage: A Life that continued to live.

legacy.content: Some lives are remembered for what they achieved. Others are remembered for how they made people feel. Balarama Krishna belonged to the latter. He did not live a life surrounded by titles or great possessions. He lived a life built on hard work, honesty, responsibility, family and relationships. He was an electrician by profession, but that was only one part of who he was. To his family, he was the person who carried their responsibilities on his shoulders. To the people of his village, he was someone they could trust. To many, he was not even addressed by his name—he was Babai, Mamayya, Bava, Tatayya—names that reflected the place he held in their hearts. He had dreams of his own. He once wished to serve the nation by joining the Indian Army. Although a fracture prevented that dream from becoming reality, the qualities behind that dream—discipline, courage, determination and a willingness to serve—remained with him throughout his life. His life was also made of simple things. A cup of tea. A newspaper at a familiar tea shop. A day's work. A conversation with someone he knew. A responsibility fulfilled. A family waiting for him to come home. These ordinary moments became extraordinary because they were his. And then, when life placed him in his final and most difficult moment, he gave one more thing. He gave what he could still give. Through organ and eye donation, his final act became a gift to others. His liver, two kidneys and two eyes were donated, giving five individuals the opportunity for a second life or restored vision. His heart could not ultimately be donated, despite initially positive test results, but even in that final chapter, his intention remained one of giving. His name was formally recognized by Jeevandan AP, and his eye donation was acknowledged by L V Prasad Eye Institute. But perhaps the greatest measure of his legacy is not written on a certificate. It lives in the people who remember him. In the family that carries his values forward. In the people who still remember calling him by affectionate names. In the stories that will be told about him. And in the lives that continue because, even in death, he gave something of himself to others. His life reminds us that a meaningful life does not have to be extraordinary in the eyes of the world. Sometimes, it is enough to work honestly, love deeply, carry your responsibilities, treat people with kindness, and leave behind something that helps another person live. That was his legacy. Kanagala Balarama Krishna may no longer walk among us, but the values he lived by, the relationships he built, the memories he created, and the lives touched by his final act continue to carry his presence forward. His journey ended. His legacy did not.

closing.title: A Final Message From Your Family
closing.subtitle: Dear Nanna,
closing.message: We still find it difficult to believe that you are no longer going to walk through that door. There are moments when we still expect you to come home after work. There are moments when we hear something and instinctively think, 'We should tell Nanna about this.' And then, for a moment, reality reminds us that you are no longer here in the way you once were. We miss you. We miss your presence. We miss your voice. We miss the way you responded when we called you 'Nanna.' We miss the ordinary things that we once never thought we would have to miss. You spent your life working for us. You carried the responsibilities of our family without making them feel like burdens. You worked as an electrician, travelled for work, built relationships wherever you went, and returned home to the family that was always waiting for you. You taught us many things without sitting down to teach us. You taught us through the way you lived. You showed us the value of honesty. You showed us the meaning of hard work. You showed us how important it is to stand by our family. And perhaps most importantly, you showed us how to remain connected to people. You were called Babai, Mamayya, Bava and Tatayya by people who were not merely acquaintances, but people who felt that you belonged to them. That was something special about you. You made people feel that they were family. We will always remember the simple things that made you who you were. Your love for tea. Your habit of sitting at tea shops and reading the newspaper. Your everyday routines. Your work. Your conversations. Your presence at home. We never imagined that these ordinary memories would one day become some of our most precious possessions. And then came 3 August 2025. A day that began like every other day. You left home after your morning routine, telling Amma that you would return and have your breakfast. We never imagined that those would become the last ordinary words of that kind we would remember. The days that followed changed our lives forever. We prayed. We hoped. We waited. We refused to believe that we could lose you. Even when the doctors gave us almost no hope, our hearts continued to hold on to that tiny possibility that you would somehow come back to us. And when that hope finally disappeared, we were left with a pain that words cannot explain. But even in that darkest moment, something beautiful came from the person you had always been. You gave. You gave your organs. You gave your eyes. And through that final act, five individuals were given the opportunity for a second life or restored vision. We lost you. But somewhere in this world, lives continue because of you. That thought does not erase our pain. It never will. But it gives us something to hold on to. It gives us a reason to feel proud of you even through our tears. Nanna, we wish you had stayed. We wish we could have had more mornings with you. More conversations. More cups of tea. More ordinary days. More moments that we would never have realized were precious until they were gone. But since we cannot change what happened, we will carry you with us in the only way we can. We will remember you. We will speak about you. We will tell your stories. We will preserve your memories. We will carry forward the values you lived by. And whenever someone asks us who you were, we will never simply say: 'He was our father.' We will say: He was a hardworking man. He was an honest man. He was a loving husband. He was a devoted father. He was a brother. He was a friend. He was Babai, Mamayya, Bava and Tatayya to many. And in the end, he became a giver of life. You may no longer be here to hear us say it. But we hope that wherever your memory lives, you know this: We are proud of you, Nanna. We love you. We miss you. And we will carry you with us—for the rest of our lives. Until our last breath, you will remain a part of us.
closing.continuation: His story continues in the lives and memories he left behind.
